note: Clark County area near Kahoka with a 108-acre fishing lake. MDC allows camping on or beside every gravel parking lot and maps eleven camping spots: the main one is a small gravel loop on a wooded point of the lake's north shore, east of the boat ramp, marked for individual campsites; the rest are lots around the lake and in the separate west tract by US 136. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: page 'Camping: Open Camping-Walk/Float/Backpack(no Deer/Turkey); Individual Campsites'; brochure 'Camping is allowed on or adjacent to all graveled area parking lots', 14 days in 30; map (08/17) Primitive Camping Area + one Primitive-Individual Camp Sites symbol; GIS 11 points. Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights manual. PIN on GIS 497 = a minor roadside lot in the west tract 6.5 km from the lake; move to the lake's individual-campsite loop (GIS 381) 40.5030,-91.7681. Waterfront lead for that loop (lakeview candidate). Phone matches.
flags: INCLUSION/FIT: area page 'Things to Do When You Visit': 'Camping: Open Camping-Walk/Float/Backpack(no Deer/Turkey); Individual Campsites'. Brochure: 'Camping is allowed on or adjacent to all graveled area parking lots. No unattended open campfires allowed. Groups of more than 10 campers require a special use permit. Stays are limited to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period.' Map (08/17) legend has both 'Primitive Camping Area' (red tent triangles, one beside nearly every lot) and 'Primitive-Individual Camp Sites' (one symbol, on the lake's north shore east of the fishing dock); GIS 27 has 11 'Primitive Camping Area' points (381, 495-504), all but 381 beside a GIS lot. Designated points beside lots: stays. No horse camp, ford or rig wording.

PIN (main camp): stored 40.45152,-91.80621 = GIS 497 beside lot 14, a ~25 x 30 m gravel lot on a county gravel road in the separate west tract by US 136 (cemetery across the road) - a minor spot 6.5 km from the lake. The lake camps are the area's centre (boat ramp, fishing dock, privies, potable water on the map). Move to the individual-campsite loop at GIS 381: a gravel teardrop loop ~45 m across at the end of a spur on a wooded point of the north shore, 40.5030,-91.7681 (GIS 381 itself, 40.50271,-91.76834, is on a cleared spot on the loop's south edge).

CLUSTERS / NO SPLIT proposed: lake north shore 381 (individual-site loop), 502 (beside the paved boat-ramp loop lot 9, ~200 m W), 501 (lot 8 at the end of the west spur, 0.6 km W), 503 (lot 7, 1.2 km NW); 500 (lot 10 by the marsh, 0.5 km SE) and 499 (lot 6, 1.6 km S, below the dam); the range tract 495/496 (lots 11/12 by the shooting and archery ranges, 2.6-3.0 km SW); the west tract 497 (old pin), 498, 504 by US 136 (6-7 km SW). The west tract has its own roads and entrance, but its three spots are small roadside lots, so no split is proposed; if AWH wants it listed, the candidate is 'Fox Valley Lake Conservation Area (west tract)' at 40.45152,-91.80621 (nothing else in campgrounds.json within 3 km of either point).

WATERFRONT LEAD (for the moved pin; the stored not waterfront was read at the west-tract lot, where there is no water): the 381 loop sits on a point of the 108-acre lake, its west and south edges ~15-30 m from the water with a band of shoreline trees between (imagery estimate, 0.28 m/px; Overpass did not answer). Trees, not open ground, lie between, so not on-water; a filtered lake view from the loop is likely but not confirmed by any MDC photo -> lakeview candidate for AWH, otherwise not waterfront stays.
